gloss: to make the first move; to take the initiative

definitions.gloss: to make the first move; to take the initiative; to act preemptively
definitions.explanation: To take action before the other party does, gaining a strategic advantage. Originally from shogi/go terminology where 先手 is the player who moves first.

examples.japanese: {先手|せんて}を{打|う}って{交渉|こうしょう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: I took the initiative and started negotiations.

examples.japanese: {競合|きょうごう}より{先手|せんて}を{打|う}って{新商品|しんしょうひん}を{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: We got ahead of our competitors by announcing the new product first.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}が{大|おお}きくなる{前|まえ}に{先手|せんて}を{打|う}って{対策|たいさく}を{講|こう}じるべきだ。
examples.english: We should take preemptive action and implement countermeasures before the problem grows.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
From board game terminology. In shogi and go, {先手|せんて} refers to the player who moves first, which is considered an advantage. {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ means to secure that first-mover advantage.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ vs. {後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}る: Opposite expressions. {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ is proactive; {後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}る is reactive and disadvantageous.
- {先|さき}を{越|こ}す: To get ahead of someone — focuses on outpacing rather than strategic positioning.
- {先制|せんせい}する: To strike first, to preempt — more aggressive, often used in military or sports contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {先手|せんて}を{打|う}って{対応|たいおう}する (to respond proactively)
- {先手|せんて}を{打|う}って{動|うご}く (to act preemptively)
